question: Let $E_1,E_2,E_3$ be three non-empty events forming a partition of a sample space $S$, and let $A$ be an event with non-zero probability. Establish the expression for $P(E_2|A)$ using the theorem of total probability and Bayes’ theorem, and hence evaluate it when $P(E_1)=\frac{1}{2}$, $P(E_2)=\frac{1}{3}$, $P(E_3)=\frac{1}{6}$, $P(A|E_1)=\frac{1}{5}$, $P(A|E_2)=\frac{1}{2}$ and $P(A|E_3)=\frac{3}{4}$.
explanation:
Formation of the Required Expression
Since $E_1,E_2,E_3$ form a partition of the sample space, the theorem of total probability gives
$$P(A)=P(E_1)P(A|E_1)+P(E_2)P(A|E_2)+P(E_3)P(A|E_3).$$

By Bayes’ theorem,
$$P(E_2|A)=\frac{P(E_2)P(A|E_2)}{P(A)}.$$
Therefore,
$$P(E_2|A)=\frac{P(E_2)P(A|E_2)}{P(E_1)P(A|E_1)+P(E_2)P(A|E_2)+P(E_3)P(A|E_3)}.$$

Evaluation
Using the given values,
$$P(A)=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{3}{4}.$$
Thus,
$$P(A)=\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{8}.$$
Taking the LCM as $120$,
$$P(A)=\frac{12+20+15}{120}=\frac{47}{120}.$$
Also,
$$P(E_2)P(A|E_2)=\frac{1}{3}\times\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{6}.$$
Hence,
$$P(E_2|A)=\frac{\frac{1}{6}}{\frac{47}{120}}=\frac{1}{6}\times\frac{120}{47}=\frac{20}{47}.$$

Final Result
Therefore, $P(E_2|A)=\frac{20}{47}$.
